extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards from the MPEP for evaluating requests, petitions, statements, and amendments in ex parte reexamination of U.S. patents, including filing, timing, form, and substantive criteria for granting or denying reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for vacating a reexamination order (A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination order may be vacated where: (A) the request was filed more than one year after the requester was served with a complaint alleging infringement and all claims of the patent were not held invalid by a final Federal Court decision after all appeals; (B) all claims of the patent were held invalid by a final decision of a Federal Court after all appeals; (C) reexamination was ordered for the wrong patent; (D) reexamination was ordered based on a duplicate copy of the request; or (E) the reexamination order is based wholly on the same question of patentability raised by the prior art previously considered in an earlier concluded examination of the patent (e.g., application which matured into the patent, a prior reexamination, an interference proceeding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As to (E) note In re Recreative Technologies Corp., 83 F.3d 1394, 38 USPQ2d 1776 (Fed. Cir. 1996). See MPEP § 2242 II.A for criteria for vacating a reexamination order in view of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party opposition to 37 CFR 1.181 petition (timing and single submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 is filed to vacate a reexamination order, the requester (if present) may file a single submission in opposition to the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reexamination proceedings are conducted with special dispatch, any opposition by the third party requester must be filed within two weeks of the date upon which a copy of the original 1.181 petition was served on the third party requester. It is advisable that the requester immediately notify the Central Reexamination Unit and the Special Program Examiner by telephone and, whenever possible, file the opposition by facsimile transmission. The filing of a 1.181 petition to vacate an ultra vires reexamination order is limited to a single submission, even if an opposition is filed by a third party requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of prior art submitted after the order
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior art citations under 37 CFR 1.501 submitted after the date of the decision on the order should be retained in a separate file by the Technology Center until the reexamination proceeding is concluded, at which time the prior art citation is entered of record on the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually retained by the TC Special Program Examiner; see MPEP § 2206.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision denying request — no substantial new question of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for reexamination will be denied if a substantial new question of patentability is not found based on patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner concludes no substantial new question has been raised, prepare a decision denying the reexamination request using the suggested form paragraph. The decision should be mailed and the reexamination file processed as concluded if no petition is timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required explanations in denial decision for each cited reference (A–D)
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision denying the request must indicate, for each patent and printed publication cited in the request, why the citation is: (A) cumulative to the teachings of the art cited in the earlier concluded examination; (B) not available against the claims (e.g., due to date or not a publication); (C) not important to a reasonable examiner in deciding patentability even though not cumulative and available; or (D) one cited in the record of the patent and barred by the guidelines in MPEP § 2242 II.A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should also respond to the substance of each argument raised by the requester based on patents or printed publications. Grounds not based on prior art patents or printed publications (e.g., public use, on sale under 35 U.S.C. 102(b), abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c)) are improper for reexamination and are not considered (see 37 CFR 1.552(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question of patentability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference raises a substantial new question of patentability if it teaches matter not present in the earlier prosecution and there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the teaching important in deciding patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in MPEP illustrate assessing novelty of teaching (e.g., spring-supported extruder at 30 degrees not present in earlier prosecution) and whether a reference is merely a substantial equivalent of prior art already of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition under 37 CFR 1.515(c) — review and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The requester may seek review by petition to the Director under 1.181 within one month of the mailing date of the examiner’s determination refusing ex parte reexamination; the petition must comply with 1.181(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no petition is timely filed or the decision on petition affirms that no substantial new question has been raised, the determination is final and nonappealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of petitions and TC Director review (de novo)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition seeking review of the examiner’s determination is filed, the reexamination file is forwarded to the TC Director for decision and the TC Director will review de novo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each TC Director decision shall conclude: 'This decision is final and nonappealable. 37 CFR 1.515(c). No further communication on this matter will be acknowledged or considered.' If the petition is granted, the decision should set a 2-month period for filing a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 and the file returned for reassignment to another examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassignment rule after grant of petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Reassignment of the reexamination proceeding will be the general rule after a petition is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only in exceptional circumstances (e.g., no other examiner available and capable) will the case remain with the examiner who denied the request. Under normal circumstances, the proceeding will not be reassigned to an SPE, primary examiner, or assistant examiner who was involved in any part of the original examination; exceptions may be made when the original examiner is the only one with adequate knowledge of the technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner statement timing and content (37 CFR 1.530)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in §1.510(e), no statement or other response by the patent owner shall be filed prior to the determinations made in accordance with §1.515 or §1.520. If reexamination is ordered, the order will set a period of not less than two months from the date of the order within which the patent owner may file a statement on the new question of patentability, including any proposed amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any statement must clearly point out why the subject matter as claimed is not anticipated or rendered obvious by the prior art patents or printed publications, alone or in reasonable combinations. Where the request was filed by a third party requester, any statement must be served upon the requester in accordance with §1.248. First extensions may be granted up to one month for good and sufficient reasons; further extensions only in extraordinary situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service proof and consequences for patent owner statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner must serve a copy of the statement on the requester (unless requester is the owner); proof of service must be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proof of service appears omitted, Reexamination Clerk should contact the patent owner to obtain a supplemental paper indicating manner and date of service; if owner cannot be contacted, Clerk contacts requester to verify service. If the 2-month period has expired and requester has not been served, the owner’s statement may be considered inappropriate and denied consideration (see MPEP § 2267).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester reply period under 37 CFR 1.535
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for response by the requester for a reply under 37 CFR 1.535 is 2 months from the owner’s service date, not 2 months from the date the patent owner’s statement was received in the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reexamination — general manner (37 CFR 1.530(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed amendment in an ex parte or inter partes reexamination proceeding is made by filing a paper directing the specific changes to the patent specification, including claims, or drawings. Amendments may be submitted with a patent owner request, as part of a patent owner statement, or where permitted during prosecution under §1.550(a) or §1.937.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification changes (other than claims) must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph including markings per 1.530(f). An entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presenting its text. Precise insertion point must be identified. Markings compare to the original patent, not prior amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to claims — content and markings (37 CFR 1.530(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each patent claim being proposed to be changed and of each new claim being proposed to be added. For any changed claim, a parenthetical expression 'amended,' 'twice amended,' etc., should follow the claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each changed or added claim must include markings pursuant to 1.530(f) (brackets for deletions, underlining for additions), except that a claim may be canceled by a statement canceling the claim without presenting the text. Added claims may require excess claim fees per 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings amendments procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing proposed changes in red for examiner approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon approval, only new sheets of drawings including the changes and in compliance with §1.84 must be filed. Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended,' added figures as 'New,' and canceled figures surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal paper requirements for reexamination filings (37 CFR 1.52(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers (other than drawings) submitted on paper or by facsimile to become part of the permanent USPTO records must be on sheets the same size, not permanently bound, white, flexible/strong/smooth/non-shiny/durable, and either DIN A4 or 8.5x11 inches with specified margins, written on only one side in portrait, and plainly legible in permanent dark ink or equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheets should permit direct reproduction by photographic, electrostatic, photo-offset, microfilming, and electronic capture. Papers should have no holes. If noncompliant papers are submitted, applicant/patent owner/requester will be notified and given time to provide substitute papers to avoid abandonment/termination/refusal of consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and spacing/format requirements (37 CFR 1.52(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application or proceeding and any amendments must comply with 1.52(a) and be in the English language or accompanied by an English translation. The specification and amendments must be 1.5 or double spaced, in a nonscript type font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, or Courier, preferably font size 12; may be no smaller than 0.21 cm (0.08 inch) high), and only a single column of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claim(s) must commence on a separate physical sheet or electronic page. The abstract must commence on a separate sheet or be submitted as the first page in reissue or reexamination proceedings. Noncompliant submissions will trigger a notice and opportunity to correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims and explanation of support for claim changes (37 CFR 1.530(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims, the filer must supply, on pages separate from the changes, the status (pending or canceled) as of the amendment date of all patent claims and all added claims, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes to the claims made by the amendment paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for changes (37 CFR 1.530(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes relative to the patent being reexamined which are made to the specification, including the claims, must include the following markings: (1) matter to be omitted must be enclosed in brackets; and (2) matter to be added must be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All bracketing and underlining are made in comparison to the original patent; newly added paragraphs must be submitted completely underlined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of patent claims preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered. The numbering of any claims added in the reexamination proceeding must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope and new matter prohibition (37 CFR 1.530(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent, and no amendment other than cancellation of claims will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate issued after the expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are treated as entered for prosecution purposes if timely and compliant, but proposed amendments are not effective until the reexamination certificate is issued. See MPEP §2258 for enlargement-of-scope discussion and MPEP §2270 for new matter handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment entry and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and are formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b), and contain all fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c), will be entered in the reexamination file pursuant to MPEP § 2234.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If adding claims, excess claim fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (4) may apply. Amended or new claims which broaden the scope of a claim should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305; the test for enlargement is the same as that under the 2-year limitation for reissue applications adding enlarging claims (In re Freeman).
